semanticDifferences: Root renders no HTML element: React Aria's Select root was one <div> carrying the payload's classes and the state attributes. The wrapper is now provided by a merged Field.Root element (render={<div …/>}) that also keeps data-disabled/data-invalid/data-dirty/data-touched/data-filled/data-focused for the group-* selectors the payload's Label/HintText use; data-open/data-focused/data-focus-visible are re-applied by the unit because React Aria exposed them on that element.

Value selection is a value, not a key: React Aria addressed options by `id`/`selectedKey`. Base UI stores the item itself, so Select passes the item object and sets isItemEqualToValue to compare `id` — the payload's selectedKey/defaultSelectedKey/onSelectionChange keep working through a key<->item bridge built from the `items` prop (an unknown key resolves to a bare `{ id }` item).

Item identity: React Aria's ListBoxItem `id` was the collection key; Base UI keys options by `value` and renders `id` as a DOM attribute, so SelectItem keeps `id` as the payload's key, feeds it into `value`, and does not forward it to the DOM. `textValue` maps to Base UI's `label` (typeahead).

that does not render its children as its element content: the payload's outer/inner split (outer w-full py-px px-1, inner rounded hover/press surface) is reproduced with `render={(props, state) =>

}` so the role/aria/data attributes stay on the outer element.
Options are rendered by the caller, so the payload's `children` render function is projected over the `items` prop (`items.map(item => children(item))`); Base UI's Select has no Collection part.

React Aria's ListBoxItem supplied the option's accessible name/description through its Text slots (`labelProps.id`/`descriptionProps.id` -> aria-labelledby/aria-describedby). SelectItem regenerates those ids (useId) on the label/description spans and sets the same ARIA relations.

Positioner default `alignItemWithTrigger` is true (popup overlaps the trigger); the payload expects a detached bottom-start dropdown, so it is set to false and the popover's placement/offset are expressed as side='bottom' align='start' sideOffset=4 collisionPadding=0.
Popup surface vars changed: React Aria's --trigger-width/--trigger-anchor-point are Base UI's --anchor-width/--transform-origin (set on the Positioner, inherited by the Popup).
Root `modal` defaults to true in Base UI (scroll lock + blocked outside pointer interaction); React Aria's select popover was non-modal, so the unit passes modal={false} by default.

The React Aria render-prop state handed to the root `className` ({isFocused,isFocusVisible,isDisabled,isOpen,isInvalid,isRequired}) is rebuilt from the props plus locally tracked trigger focus, because Base UI's Root has no state (its state lives on the parts).

React Aria's `disabledKeys` was a collection-level prop; Base UI disables per item, so the root publishes the key set through `SelectDisabledKeysContext` (exported from select-item.tsx) and SelectItem ORs it with its own `isDisabled`.

`selectionMode`/`value`+`onChange` were not carried over: the payload's Select is single-selection (multi-value selection is MultiSelect), so only selectedKey/defaultSelectedKey/onSelectionChange (and Base UI's value/defaultValue/onValueChange shape for items) are wired.

semanticDifferences: Two independent controlled pairs replace React Aria's single ComboBox state: `value`+`onValueChange` (selection) and `inputValue`+`onInputValueChange` (typed text). The unit controls both from its own state so the payload's selectedKey/onSelectionChange and inputValue/onInputChange keep their old semantics, and so the mirrored value behind the transparent input can be rendered.

Filtering is prop-driven: React Aria filtered the collection with `defaultFilter(textValue, inputValue)`; Base UI filters `items` with its collator, so `defaultFilter` is re-expressed through Base UI's `filter(item, query, itemToString)` and the compared string is React Aria's `textValue` (label + supporting text), which also keeps the selected item visible for queries that match it.

React Aria's `menuTrigger='focus'` (open on focus) has no Base UI prop: the unit opens the popup from the input's focus handler (Base UI opens on input click and on typing by default, which covers `input`; `manual` maps to openOnInputClick={false} only).

`allowsCustomValue` has no Base UI equivalent in 1.8.0 (the docs state the Combobox does not allow free-form text as a value). The prop is kept on the type for source compatibility and does nothing; `allowsEmptyCollection` is likewise unnecessary (Base UI renders the popup/list-empty state itself).

Form submission follows Base UI: `formValue='key'` is itemToStringValue = String(id) and `formValue='text'` is the item's textValue; Base UI submits through its hidden input (React Aria used the input's own name/value).

The trigger width workaround (ResizeObserver measuring the styled group and passing an explicit popup width) is gone: Base UI anchors the Positioner to the InputGroup and the popup uses `w-(--anchor-width)`.
`shouldFocusWrap` maps to Base UI's `loopFocus`.

React Aria's single <Popover> element becomes Portal > Positioner > Popup. Like the React Aria original it is not standalone: it must be rendered inside a Popover.Root that owns the trigger (React Aria required the same overlay-trigger context).

React Aria's `placement` (and `offset`/`containerPadding`) become Base UI's `side`/`align`/`sideOffset`/`alignOffset`/`collisionPadding`; the payload's placement='bottom', offset={4}, containerPadding={0} are exported as `popoverPositionerProps` so every select-family popup anchors identically.

The popup class string (and its size-based max heights) is exported as `popoverPopupClassName(size)` and reused by select/combobox/tag-select, replacing the component wrapper those files used to render.
`triggerRef` (React Aria's overlay-to-trigger association) maps to Base UI's Positioner `anchor`.

Animation states are attributes: data-open covers the enter phase and data-ending-style the exit phase (React Aria's isEntering/isExiting render props), and `placement-*` variants are re-pointed at data-side.

Select/ComboBox only consume Field context, so every select-family root wraps its parts in Field.Root to keep the payload's Label/HintText associated with the control: Field.Label publishes the label id the trigger/input points at with aria-labelledby (React Aria's label context did this inside its own field), Field.Description does the same for the hint, and Field.Root supplies data-focused/data-invalid/data-disabled to the parts.

Field.Root renders a <div>: the payload's own wrapper (className, style, ref) is merged into it with `render`, so the DOM keeps one root element. Field.Root has no `required` prop (required lives on the control), so `isRequired` goes to the root component only and the Label keeps its explicit isRequired asterisk.

migrationRecord.publicComponent: Select (+ Select.Item, Select.ComboBox, SelectContext, sizes, CommonProps, SelectItemType), Popover, ComboBox, MultiSelect (+ MultiSelect.Item/.Footer/.EmptyState), TagSelect (+ TagSelect.Item, TagSelectBase, TagSelectTagsValue)
migrationRecord.existingUntitledUiBehavior: Select is React Aria's Select wrapped in a styled trigger button (avatar/icon + label + supporting text or placeholder + chevron), a Label above and a HintText below, with the options rendered through a ListBox inside a Popover; items are keyed by `id`, carry avatarUrl/label/supportingText/icon/isDisabled, and every item draws its own hover/selected surface plus a checkmark, checkbox or no indicator. ComboBox adds a styled Group with a leading icon, a transparent input over a mirrored value (label + supporting text in two colours) and a ⌘K shortcut badge. MultiSelect is a dialog-style popup with a search field, a multiple listbox, an empty state and a reset/select-all footer, reporting a count in its trigger. TagSelect keeps its selected items as chips inside the input group (avatar + label + remove button, valueFormatter), filters out already-selected items, and navigates between chips and input with the arrow keys.
migrationRecord.canonicalBehavioralContract: Keys stay the public selection vocabulary (selectedKey/defaultSelectedKey/onSelectionChange, Selection = 'all' | Set<Key>), the trigger/value/option rendering and their class strings are unchanged, React Aria's render-prop state shapes survive for every public className/style/children function, option typeahead matches the same textValue, filtering matches React Aria's collator `contains` semantics, the popup is a non-modal bottom-start dropdown sized to the trigger, every Label/HintText stays associated with its control, and the exported symbols/props/defaults of the six files are unchanged.
migrationRecord.baseUiCompositionChosen: Field.Root (merged wrapper) > Select.Root > (Label?, Trigger > Value(> Icon), Portal > Positioner > Popup > List > Item*) + HintText; ComboBox = Field.Root > Combobox.Root > InputGroup (combobox.tsx) or Trigger + Portal > Positioner > Popup > (Input?, Empty?, List, footer) (multi-select) > HintText; TagSelect = Field.Root > Combobox.Root(multiple) > InputGroup(tags + Input) + Portal > Positioner > Popup > List. Contexts: the payload's SelectContext (size) is unchanged, with a new SelectDisabledKeysContext for `disabledKeys` and a TagSelectContext carrying the tag callbacks.
migrationRecord.whyNotOneToOne: React Aria composes one element per concern and hands state to render props (Select renders a div that is the field, the trigger, the value, the popup and the listbox at once; ComboBox merges selection and input text into one state), while Base UI splits each family into parts whose state lives in data attributes and whose popup owns Portal/Positioner/Popup. The payload's public API is key-based and render-prop shaped, so each file keeps its prop names and remaps them onto the part composition, re-creating the state those render props used to receive and bridging keys <-> item values with id equality.
